long_biography.plain_text:
Hotelier Andreas Panayiotou arranged his working day around spoken information. His assistant read emails aloud and he dictated replies, while lawyers and accountants handled specialist documents. He relied on a trained memory for figures and simplified problems before making decisions, adapting his business routine to a lifelong difficulty with reading.

He spoke publicly about that difficulty to support a London literacy campaign, describing the humiliation he had experienced at school and the value of early help for children. Learning to fly supplied a different incentive: determined to qualify as a pilot, he memorised the training manual at seventeen.
